Photograph: Jung Yeon-Je/AFP/Getty Images North Korea North Korea fires 10 missiles day after Trump curtails South Korea joint drills Launches, detected by South Korea and Japan, came after US scaled back exercises with South Korea in apparent overture to Kim Jong-un Associated Press Thu 20 Aug 2026 06.25 EDT Last modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 07.30 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google North Korea has launched about 10 short-range ballistic missiles towards the sea, South Korea’s military said, a day after Pyongyang shrugged off Donald Trump’s order to scale back US military drills with South Korea in an apparent attempt to resume diplomacy. The joint chiefs of staff said the missiles were launched from the region of Pyongyang at around 5pm (08.00 GMT) on Thursday towards North Korea’s eastern waters. The military said South Korea had bolstered its surveillance and was closely coordinating information on the launches with the US and Japan. Trump’s move to gut South Korea alliance is ‘inane, haphazard decision’, lawmakers say Read more South Korea’s presidential national security council held an emergency meeting, after which it issued a statement urging North Korea to halt ballistic missile launches, which are banned under UN security council resolutions. The Japanese prime minister’s office said earlier that it had detected a suspected missile launch. On Wednesday, the South Korean and US militaries said they were scaling back their 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises. Donald Trump had ordered the Pentagon to “substantially reduce” the exercises just before they began on Monday. Explaining his reasons for the decision, the US president cited what he said was a good relationship with North Korea’s leader, Kim Jong-un, and South Korea’s refusal to support him over the war against Iran. Kim Yo-jong, the influential sister of the North Korean leader, dismissed Trump’s overture on Wednesday, saying it was not worthy of comment. “The provocative, aggressive nature of the drills won’t change even though their duration and size were reduced,” she said. “If the US calculates that it can propagate its recent measure as one of so-called good faith, they will not get the desired answer.” She highlighted a series of other military drills carried out by the US and South Korea earlier this year and South Korea’s push to introduce nuclear-powered submarines. However, Kim Yo-jong refrained from the typical North Korean reaction of fiery rhetoric, and said personal relations between her brother and Trump were “still excellent”. That could signal a desire by Pyongyang to wait for Trump to make bigger concessions before returning to talks. She denied Trump’s claim that Kim Jong-un had responded to his request for a conversation. When asked by reporters on Wednesday if he would be meeting Kim Jong-un this year, Trump said: “Yeah, I will be.” He would not answer a question about whether he was exchanging letters with Kim, but said he got along with him. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: 1:02 News helicopter crash kills at least three people in Los Angeles – video Los Angeles NBC helicopter crash in LA kills at least three people with others injured Accident occurred as news crews in Los Angeles were covering a bus crash that had killed at least two people hours earlier The Associated Press Wed 16 Sep 2026 00.32 EDT First published on Tue 15 Sep 2026 23.58 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A news helicopter crash in a Los Angeles neighborhood has killed at least three people, after it came to the ground and burst into flames near the site of a bus crash that occurred hours earlier. The helicopter crashed near a one-storey commercial building in the neighborhood of Chatsworth in the San Fernando Valley, as news crews were covering the bus crash that left at least two people dead and six others injured, according the Los Angeles Fire Department. An NBC4 Los Angeles anchor at the station confirmed during a live broadcast that its chopper went down just before 7pm. At least one person killed in the helicopter crash was outside in the parking lot next to the commercial building, Capt Branden Silverman, a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Fire Department, said during a news conference. It was unclear if the other two who were killed were on the ground or inside the aircraft. One person was taken to the hospital, but their condition was not immediately clear. View image in fullscreen Investigators work the scene after the helicopter crashed near a bus crash in Chatsworth, a neighborhood in Los Angeles, Tuesday, Sept. 15, 2026. Photograph: Ethan Swope/AP “We’re trying to determine how many patients were inside the helicopter,” said Silverman, who described the helicopter as “pretty well destroyed” and adding that officials would be sorting through the rubble to see how many victims were on board. At least four cars and two storage containers on the ground burned after the helicopter caught fire, which was quickly put out, according to officials. More than 50 firefighters responded to the helicopter crash, according to the fire department. About two hours before the crash, an SUV slammed into the middle of a city bus, killing at least two people and injuring six others. Photos and videos online showed half of the SUV lodged into the side of an MTA bus. The helicopter crashed about a 1.5 miles from the bus crash. The National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration said it will be investigating the cause of the helicopter crash. https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2.text: Fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and government forces supported by Saudi Arabia has killed 154 people in the past two days, military sources told the AFP news agency, and has sparked a refugee crisis. “The death toll from Saudi airstrikes, clashes and artillery fire in the governorates of Taiz, Al-Jawf, Marib and Saada stands at 118,” Houthi military sources said, while government sources reported 36 killed in their “ranks”, according to AFP. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that started in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the internationally recognised government from Sanaa, the country’s capital, driving it south towards Aden. A Saudi-led coalition of Arab states subsequently intervened on behalf of the ousted government, with a mostly aerial campaign that was condemned for its deadly impact on the civilians of Yemen. Photograph: Rocco Fazzari/AAP New South Wales Beau Lamarre-Condon denies being ‘obsessed’ with Jesse Baird as double murder trial continues Former police officer tells jury he joked about being ‘white girl crazy’ with friends as lawyer questions him over start of relationship with Baird Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Kat Wong Mon 9 Nov 2026 19.53 EST First published on Mon 9 Nov 2026 19.18 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Beau Lamarre-Condon has denied being “obsessed” with Jesse Baird from the start of their relationship, telling a court he would have liked the TV presenter even if he was “a garbage cleaner”. The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024. He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter. Sitting in the witness box for the fourth day, Lamarre-Condon was grilled by crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC about his relationship with Baird. The former officer told the NSW supreme court he would meet up with Baird in October and November 2022 for sexual encounters before the pair began going on romantic dates in December of that year. Under cross-examination on Tuesday, Hatfield asked Lamarre-Condon: “You were obsessed with him right from the start?” Lamarre-Condon denied this, telling the jury: “I never cared about showing Jesse off. I wanted Jesse to meet my friends because I thought he was genuine”. “Jesse Baird could have been a garbage cleaner… I liked Jesse for who he was as a person,” Lamarre-Condon said. Asked by Hatfield if Lamarre-Condon was “obsessed” with Baird in February and March 2023, the accused responded: “I don’t agree with ‘obsessed’. Smitten? Yes. Obsessed? no.” View image in fullscreen Supplied images of Luke Davies (left) and Jesse Baird (right). Composite: Supplied/NSW Supreme Court Hatfield pointed to messages between Lamarre-Condon and his friends sent around the time the pair began going on dates, where the officer says: “it sounds crazy, I love him”. Lamarre-Condon responded: “I say ‘I love you’ to all my friends and to people like that all the time.” “That’s different to saying I’m ‘in’ love with him,” he said. Asked whether he was insecure about the relationship and whether Baird liked him, Lamarre-Condon said his response was “natural” and sometimes occurred when the TV presenter did not reply to his messages straight away. “I would always joke [with my friends], ‘we’re white girl crazy’,” Lamarre-Condon told the jury. “It means we should stop being in our head and second-guessing ourselves.” He told the court he would make jokes and have “banter” with his female friends, not his heterosexual male friends, telling each other things like: “you’re a crazy bitch”. Lamarre-Condon told the court he had looked through Baird’s phone, using it to unfollow people, when the pair went on a brief holiday to a cabin in regional NSW. “In relation to breaching his privacy and, yes, his trust I did unfollow two to three people,” he said. “I believe curiosity just got the best of me. “Our relationship was progressing, I just kind of wanted to see where he was at … if he was also messaging other guys romantically… I’m not making excuses for my behaviour.” Later, when the prosecution attempted to go through messages between Lamarre-Condon and one of his friends, the officer directly addressed Hatfield, telling him: “Mr Crown, I think you’re trying to mislead me here”. Justice Natalie Adams interjected, telling Lamarre-Condon to “just answer the question”. “If the crown is misleading you, [the defence lawyer] will object,” she said. The trial continues.
